title: Protons, neutrons and electrons: inside the atom
examples: What are protons, neutrons and electrons?

layers.label: Mostly empty space
layers.note: Most of the atom is nothing at all.

explain.say: Every atom in your body, your phone and the air is built from just three kinds of tiny particle. Look at the board. This is one atom, drawn as a ball. Let us peel it from the outside in.

draw.text: Protons, neutrons and electrons: inside the atom

layers.label: Mostly empty space
layers.note: Most of the atom is nothing at all.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: an atom. Look at the nucleus, the proton and the neutron. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Protons, neutrons and electrons: inside the atom

explain.say: See the outer part lit up? That is where electrons whizz around. An electron is a super-light particle with a negative charge. Charge is a kind of electric push and pull. Have you felt a static shock from your jumper? That is electrons moving!

layers.label: Mostly empty space
layers.note: Most of the atom is nothing at all.

explain.say: Now look right in the middle, at the nucleus. It holds protons, which have a positive charge, and neutrons, which have no charge at all. They are packed together tightly. Which particle do you think is the heaviest?

layers.label: Mostly empty space
layers.note: Most of the atom is nothing at all.

explain.say: Look at the table on the board. Protons and neutrons weigh about the same, but an electron is about 1,840 times lighter. So almost all the mass of an atom is in its tiny nucleus. Are you surprised?

Great work! One more secret: an atom has as many protons as electrons, so the plus and minus charges cancel out. The number of protons decides the element. Wow: every atom with 6 protons is carbon, in a diamond or in your pencil.

faq.a: Electrons move around the nucleus in shells. They have a negative charge and are very light, and they are the particles that take part in chemical reactions.
The nucleus holds protons, which are positive, and neutrons, which have no charge. Together they make up almost all of the atom's mass.
asks: What is the nucleus made of?

faq.a: An atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. Each proton is +1 and each electron is -1, so the charges cancel out.
asks: Why does an atom have no overall charge?

faq.a: Protons and neutrons have almost the same mass, with neutrons very slightly heavier. An electron is about 1,840 times lighter than a proton.
asks: Relative masses of protons, neutrons and electrons

faq.q: What decides which element an atom is?
faq.a: The number of protons, called the atomic number. Every atom with 8 protons is oxygen, and every atom with 79 protons is gold.

facts: A proton is about 1,836 times as heavy as an electron.

quiz.why: Neutrons are neutral: they have no charge.

wrong.0: An electron has a negative charge.
wrong.2: A proton has a positive charge.

quiz.say: An atom has 11 protons. How many electrons does the neutral atom have?
quiz.show: An atom has 11 protons. How many electrons does the neutral atom have?
quiz.why: A neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons.

wrong.1: That would leave an extra negative charge.
wrong.2: Electrons equal protons; you do not double them.
